claims.text: The half-open search interval preserves the lower-bound invariant.

teaching.content: Find the first element greater than or equal to the target, not merely any matching element. The candidate interval [lo,hi) shrinks while retaining this boundary. Predict the insertion index before showing steps.

The loop maintains: indices < lo are less than the target, and indices >= hi are greater than or equal to the target. Each update strictly reduces hi-lo, ensuring termination. At lo=hi the unique boundary is the lower bound.

assessments.prompt: Prove lower-bound binary search correct for duplicates and an empty array.
assessments.solution: Initially [lo,hi)=[0,n), so both outside assertions hold vacuously. When a[mid]<x, all indices <=mid are below x and lo moves to mid+1; otherwise all indices >=mid have values >=x and hi moves to mid. Every iteration decreases the nonnegative interval length hi-lo. At termination lo=hi, with all earlier elements <x and all later ones >=x; this is the first qualifying index, or n if no such element exists. For an empty array, lo=hi=0 immediately.

cards.front: Which invariant does lower-bound binary search maintain?
cards.answer: Indices before lo have values < target; indices at/after hi have values >= target.

interactions.prediction_prompt: Predict the first index with a value at least the target.
interactions.feedback_rule: Compare each updated interval to the invariant.
interactions.transfer_prompt: Which branch comparison would change if searching for the first value strictly greater than the target?
